svg.title: A distended abdomen: painless with bulging flanks is ascites; painful, central and tympanic is obstruction, sorted on X-ray into small bowel (adhesive after previous surgery, or non-adhesive) and large bowel (closed loop), each with presentation, numbered investigations and treatment in order, plus the FATAL signs that send any obstruction to surgery

svg.text: Distended abdomen: ASCITES or OBSTRUCTION? Then WHERE, and is it an ADHESION?

svg.text: OBSTIPATION (no stool AND no gas) is the key feature of obstruction
